name: Meal Prep Checklist
description: A step-by-step batch-cooking checklist covering planning, shopping, prepping, cooking, portioning and storage.

items.text: Choose how many meals and days you're prepping for
Pick three to five recipes that share ingredients
items.note: Overlapping ingredients cut waste and lower your grocery bill.

items.text: Balance each meal with a protein, a grain, and vegetables
Check your calendar for nights you'll be out
Note any leftovers or pantry items to use up first
List every ingredient from your chosen recipes
Check the fridge, freezer, and pantry before adding items
Group the list by aisle or category
Add staples like oil, spices, and storage bags if low
Set a budget and note any swaps for sale items
Shop the full list in one efficient trip
Wash produce and put cold items away promptly
Clear and wipe down your counters and work surface
Gather knives, cutting boards, bowls, and pans
Pull out all containers and lids you'll need
Wash and chop all vegetables at once
Trim, portion, and season proteins
Measure out grains, sauces, and dressings
Marinate proteins that need time to soak
items.note: Group similar cutting tasks to save time and dishes.

items.text: Set aside ingredients for fresh items you'll add later
Start the longest-cooking items first, like grains and roasts
Roast trays of vegetables while proteins cook
Use the oven, stovetop, and slow cooker at the same time
Cook sauces and dressings to combine later
Taste and season everything before it cools
Let cooked food cool before sealing containers
Divide meals into single-serving portions
Keep dressings and crunchy toppings separate until serving
Label each container with the meal and date
Refrigerate meals for the next three to four days
Freeze the rest in clearly dated containers
Wash dishes and reset the kitchen for the week

faq.q: How do I start meal prepping?
faq.a: Pick one prep day, plan three to five repeatable meals, shop for exactly those ingredients, then do all your chopping and cooking in one session. Start small with a few lunches before scaling up to the whole week.

faq.q: How long does meal prep take?
faq.a: A focused weekly prep session usually takes two to three hours, including cooking and cleanup. Doing all your chopping at once and cooking in batches keeps that time down as you get into a rhythm.

faq.q: How long does meal-prepped food last?
faq.a: Most cooked meals keep three to four days refrigerated in airtight containers. Cook extra and freeze portions for later in the week to avoid spoilage and waste.

faq.q: Can I print this meal prep checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each stage from planning through storage.

faq.q: What containers are best for meal prep?
faq.a: Use airtight, stackable containers in consistent sizes. Glass containers reheat well and resist stains, while compartment containers keep components separate until you're ready to eat.
